div.head: Ger 13
div.ab: [13] A he mæig findan, hwæt he mæig on byrig betan — ne ðearf he na unnyt beon, ðonne he ðær binnan bið —: oððe hus godian, rihtan ⁊ weoxian ⁊ grep hegian, dicsceard betan, hegas godian, weod wyrtwalian, betweox husan bricgian, beoddian, bencian, horsan styllan, flor feormian oððe synnes sum ðing ðe to nyte mæge.

A he mæig findan hwæt he mæig onbyrug betan ne ðearf he na unnyt beon ðonne he ðær binnan bið . oðða hus godi|an . rihtan . 7 weoxian . 7 grep hegian . dic|sceard betan . hegas godian . weod wyrtwa|lian . betweox husan bricgian . beoddian bencian . horsan styllan . flor feormian oððe synnes sum ðing ðe to nyte mæge .

A he mæig findan hwæt he mæig on byrig betan, ne ðearf he na unnyt beon ðonne he ðær binnan bið: oððe hus godian, rihtan and weoxian and grep hegian, dicsceard betan, hegas godian, weod wyrtwalian betweox husan bricgian, beoddian, bencian, horsan styllan, flor feormian oððe swilces cynnes sum ðing ðe to nyte mæge.

Immer kann er entdecken, was er im Domänengehöft bessern kann — er braucht nicht müssig zu sein, so lange er dort innerhalb ist —: entweder Häuser ausbessern, herrichten und reinigen und Graben ziehen, Grabenbruch wieder ausbessern, Gehege bessern, Unkraut jäten, zwischen Häusern pflastern, tischlern, Bänke machen, den Pferden Stall machen, Flur fegen, oder immer[?] etwas, was zu Nutzen [sein] kann.

He can always find out what he can improve in the manor — he need not be idle while he is inside it —: either repair, put right and clean houses, and dig a ditch, mend a breach in a ditch, improve fences, root out weeds, pave between the houses [with planks or stones?], make tables, make benches, make stalls for the horses, sweep the floor, or always[?] something that can [be] of use.

Always he must find what he may make better on the town, nor need he be idle when he is inside. Improve the house or straighten and cleanse, and cut drains, repair ditch-clefts, repair hedges, uproot weeds between the house and the bridge, make benches, stable horses, cleanse floors or if he [discover] something which might be needed he should do it.

He must always seek out anything he can improve out in the community, nor need he be without occupation when he is inside: he may repair the house, put things right and clean, clear the drainage ditches, fix breaks in the dikes, fix the hedges, pull weeds, lay pavement between buildings, do joiner’s work, build benches, put the horses in their stalls, wash the floors, or do anything else that might need to be done.
div.note: Liebermann suggests the original perhaps read ‘swilces cynnes’ (of such kind) or ‘sumes’ for ‘synnes’; Kluge takes ‘synnes’ as ‘always’ (after ‘gesinlice’). Liebermann compares Gerefa 8, 10, 11 and 4.

note.seg: vielleicht las Original: swilces cynnes (solcher Art) oder sumes: gewissermassen
perhaps the original read: swilces cynnes (of such a kind) or sumes: in a sense

Vgl. Gl Burg 1.—Nicht zu denken ist an byrig, das vielleicht ‘Maulbeerbaum’ (vgl. Cockayne Leechdoms II 374. III 314), nicht ‘-garten’ glossiert; diese Kultur war gewiss nicht allgemein. Gegen solche Übs. Andrews Manor 263; Stevenson in Engl. hist. rev. 1897, 491.—Zu S. 455 Z. 2 ‘das Haus in Ordnung halten, es einrichten und reinigen’{a} [falsch; bessere in ‘flechten’] Sk-Wi

Cf. Gl Burg 1.—There is no question here of the byrig that perhaps glosses ‘mulberry-tree’ (cf. Cockayne Leechdoms II 374. III 314), not ‘-garden’; this cultivation was certainly not general. Against such a translation Andrews Manor 263; Stevenson in Engl. hist. rev. 1897, 491.—On p. 455 l. 2 ‘to keep the house in order, furnish it and clean it’{a} [wrong; correct to ‘to wattle’] Sk-Wi

Nicht ‘Kaninchen’; vgl. Kluge in Engl. Stud. IX (1886) 506; mengl. grip(pe) bed. auch ‘Umschliessungsgraben’ des Gehöfts gegen aussen; Kluge übs. hegian ‘machen?’ (also wie gehegan bei Toller). Allein gehæged ‘eingeschlossen’ belegt Toller; ‘Hecken setzen längs der Wassergräben’ Sk-Wi

Not ‘rabbits’; cf. Kluge in Engl. Stud. IX (1886) 506; ME grip(pe) also means the ‘enclosing ditch’ round the outside of the farmstead; Kluge translates hegian ‘to make?’ (thus like gehegan in Toller). Toller, however, attests gehæged ‘enclosed’; ‘to plant hedges along the water-ditches’ Sk-Wi
Alongside ‘to plant’: instead of awyrtwalian ‘to uproot’; Toller

So Kluge, Pogatscher in Engl. Stud. 25, 423. An Bohlen denkt Sweet; daher das Bild von staðolfæstre brycge ofer þone glideran (schlüpfrigen) weg beim Hom. n. Wulfstan 239. Steine (Engl. Stud. XI [1888] 511; vgl. Heyne Dt. Wohnung 150) hält für unwahrscheinlich Andrews Manor 265. Doch s. Toller stanfah, -stræt, -weg; dieser hält Suppl. 109 s. v. brycgian ‘planks or stones’ möglich; ‘Bretter’ Sk-Wi; vgl.: Bremer Gesch. Qu. ed. Lappenberg: Dar weren bi den tiden noch vele straten, die bolet weren; unde men vint noch alto vele holtes under den steenweghen in manigen straten. Vgl. oferbrycgian ‘überbrücken’, Gl Brücke 1—b

Thus Kluge, Pogatscher in Engl. Stud. 25, 423. Sweet thinks of planks; hence the image of the staðolfæstre brycge ofer þone glideran (slippery) weg in Hom. n. Wulfstan 239. Stones (Engl. Stud. XI [1888] 511; cf. Heyne Dt. Wohnung 150) are thought improbable by Andrews Manor 265. But see Toller stanfah, -stræt, -weg; he considers ‘planks or stones’ possible in Suppl. 109 s. v. brycgian; ‘boards’ Sk-Wi; cf.: Bremer Gesch. Qu. ed. Lappenberg: Dar weren bi den tiden noch vele straten, die bolet weren; unde men vint noch alto vele holtes under den steenweghen in manigen straten. Cf. oferbrycgian ‘to bridge over’, Gl Brücke 1—b
Emendiere oððe [ðe]s [c]ynnes ‘oder der Art’; vgl. Forf 3, 1.—‘an irgend etwas denken’ [steht nicht da] Sk-Wi
Emend to oððe [ðe]s [c]ynnes ‘or of the kind’; cf. Forf 3, 1.—‘to think of anything’ [not in the text] Sk-Wi
